title: Processes as variable embodiments
version: Synthese 203, article 104 (2024), published 20 March 2024; DOI 10.1007/s11229-024-04505-2; open access. OA PDF URL https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s11229-024-04505-2.pdf recorded, not separately hashed.
locator: Selected: intro; §2 flight example (AZ123 clauses, 'no longer present', snowball accumulation); §3.1 processes as constituted by events (K definition, A5–A7 glosses, cognitive carving); §3.2 A8, V1'–V3' with fn 14–15, V5a'/A9–A10, A11–A12 local/global pro-tem; D5–D6; conclusions (event neutrality, accumulation summary); footnotes 10, 11, 13, 14, 15.
assumptions: Processes are variable embodiments constituted at each atomic interval by one event (functional, asymmetric, anti-transitive K(x,y,t)); manifestations accumulate (A7); parthood kept separate from constitution (A8, Baker-line); CEM adopted; events as classic perdurants, neutrality on future events (fn 10); no presence requirement for the constituting event (fn 11).
conclusion: An ongoing process token exists at t (V1') with manifestation = accumulated life 'the history of what happened until that time'; temporal location of the token is that of its manifestation (V2'); elapsed phases are timeless parts of the manifestation (A7) and manifestations of temporary parts of the token at t (A9); elapsed phases are 'no longer present' (presence idiom), and the paper leaves assessment-relative concreteness of elapsed phases undetermined.
proof_status: Selected axioms and glosses read directly and quoted; formal system not independently reconstructed or audited beyond the quoted clauses.
relevance: Primary rival account for Route A; source of the accumulation apparatus on which the candidate's conditional inference is built and of the fn-11 refutation of the pilot's fused presence claim.
limits: Not a complete reconstruction of Fine's original theory; §4–5 taxonomy read only where quoted (D5–D6, A11–A12); no claim about the authors' own temporal ontology beyond their stated neutrality.
